epics.title: Professional Profile and Service Catalog
epics.jtbd: When a professional joins the platform, I want to import my details and services from Facebook, so that I can immediately share a booking link with clients.
requirements: R1: Professional registers via Facebook login or Georgian phone number (+995).
R2: Import photos, description, and address from the professional's Facebook business page.
R3: Professional manages a catalog of services with prices in GEL (₾) and durations.
R4: System generates a public, shareable URL for the professional's profile.
R5: Customers can view the public profile and available services, satisfying the 'find the service' requirement.

slices.title: API Contract for Profile Management
slices.jtbd: When implementing the profile system for this epic, I want a shared contract, so that frontend and backend build against stable definitions.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API spec, When frontend or backend validates a request, Then it conforms to the DTOs.
Given a GET profile request, When it lacks auth, Then it succeeds for public data.

slices.title: Data Schema for Profiles and Services
slices.jtbd: When implementing storage for this epic, I want to model profiles and services, so that professional data is reliably persisted.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new professional, When saved, Then the database stores FB and phone identifiers.
Given a service addition, When saved, Then it is linked to the professional with GEL pricing.

slices.title: Profile and Facebook Import API
slices.jtbd: When implementing backend logic for this epic, I want to handle registration and FB import, so that profile data is processed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid FB token, When importing, Then photos and descriptions are fetched.
Given a valid phone login, When submitted, Then an account is provisioned.

slices.title: Mobile-First Profile UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend for this epic, I want responsive screens, so that professionals can register and customers can browse.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a mobile browser, When viewing the profile, Then the layout is responsive and usable.
Given form input, When a network error occurs, Then what the user typed survives.
Given standard navigation, When elements are focused, Then WCAG 2.1 AA standards are met including visible focus, labelled form controls, and 4.5:1 text contrast.

slices.title: Quality Assurance for Profiles
slices.jtbd: When testing the profile logic for this epic, I want to execute unit and E2E tests, so that onboarding works flawlessly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new professional test user, When E2E test runs, Then registration and FB import succeed.
Given an invalid FB token, When API test runs, Then the system gracefully handles the error.
Given a public URL, When accessed, Then the profile data matches the DB.

epics.title: Availability Calendar and MCP Booking Engine
epics.jtbd: When a customer or AI agent attempts to book, I want genuinely free slots to be securely reserved without conflicts, so that the professional's schedule is accurate.
requirements: R1: Professionals can view their schedule, block/free time, and mark appointments as no-shows.
R2: Clean REST endpoints expose search functionality and genuinely free time slots.
R3: System provides atomic temporary holds to protect against double bookings (race conditions).
R4: Booking confirmation endpoints are fully compatible with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI agents.
R5: System maintains a waiting list or immediate slot reopening mechanism when a slot frees up.

slices.title: Shared API Contract for Availability
slices.jtbd: When implementing availability features for this epic, I want a shared contract, so that client and server agree on slot representations.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the contract, When requesting slots, Then the response structure includes hold statuses.
Given a booking hold request, When validated, Then it adheres to MCP schema guidelines.

slices.title: Data Schema for Availability and Holds
slices.jtbd: When implementing the booking engine for this epic, I want to model schedules and locks, so that concurrency is handled safely.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new time slot, When saved, Then it supports state transitions (free, held, booked).
Given a no-show update, When applied, Then the historical record is maintained.

slices.title: Booking Engine Backend API
slices.jtbd: When implementing endpoints for this epic, I want to process holds and confirmations, so that AI agents and UIs can book slots.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given two simultaneous hold requests, When processed, Then exactly one succeeds.
Given an MCP confirmation, When received, Then the booking is finalized and slot locked.

slices.title: Professional Calendar Management UI
slices.jtbd: When building the calendar for this epic, I want an interface for professionals, so that they can manage their time and mark no-shows.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a destructive action like blocking a day, When triggered, Then it is confirmed before happening.
Given a schedule view, When interacting, Then visible feedback is shown for every state change.
Given the calendar UI, When interacted with, Then WCAG 2.1 AA standards are met including keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled form controls, and 4.5:1 text contrast.

slices.title: QA for Booking Engine and Concurrency
slices.jtbd: When testing the booking engine for this epic, I want to verify concurrency safety, so that double bookings are impossible.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a high load of concurrent requests for one slot, When processed, Then no double bookings occur.
Given E2E tests, When a professional blocks a slot, Then the API immediately reflects it as unavailable.

epics.title: Messaging Notifications and Reminders
epics.jtbd: When an appointment is created or approaches, I want automatic notifications and management options, so that both parties stay informed and can adjust plans.
requirements: R1: Instant booking notifications sent to professionals via Facebook Messenger and WhatsApp.
R2: Professionals can confirm or cancel bookings using buttons directly within the messenger interface.
R3: Customers receive an automatic acknowledgement immediately upon booking request submission, stating what happens next.
R4: Customers receive an automatic reminder before the appointment via SMS or email.
R5: Customers are provided a secure link to cancel or reschedule their appointment independently.

slices.title: API Contract for Reminders and Actions
slices.jtbd: When implementing notifications for this epic, I want a shared contract, so that external webhook formats and client payloads match.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the spec, When a reschedule is requested, Then the payload structure is validated.
Given a webhook definition, When implemented, Then it matches messenger requirements.

slices.title: Notification Gateway and Reminder Scheduler
slices.jtbd: When building messaging for this epic, I want to integrate external APIs, so that reminders and acknowledgements are dispatched.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new booking, When created, Then an automatic acknowledgement is queued for the customer.
Given an impending appointment, When the scheduler runs, Then a reminder SMS/email is dispatched.

slices.title: Customer Reschedule and Cancellation UI
slices.jtbd: When building the customer interface for this epic, I want a dedicated page, so that customers can alter their appointments.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the reschedule page, When accessed via secure link, Then the customer's current appointment is displayed.
Given a cancellation action, When network fails, Then visible feedback shows the failure, allowing retry.
Given the reschedule UI, When used, Then WCAG 2.1 AA standards are met including visible focus, labelled form controls, and 4.5:1 text contrast.

slices.title: QA for Notifications and Reminders
slices.jtbd: When testing notifications for this epic, I want to verify delivery paths, so that no message is lost.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a triggered reminder, When checked in the test double, Then the SMS content is verified.
Given a messenger button click simulation, When processed, Then the booking state updates to confirmed.

epics.title: Voice-Driven Booking for Drivers
epics.jtbd: When driving in Georgia, I want to verbally request and confirm bookings in Georgian, so that I can schedule hands-free.
requirements: R1: Customer records or streams a voice request in Georgian.
R2: System translates Georgian speech and extracts booking intents (service, time).
R3: System responds with a fast synthesized voice message proposing an available time.
R4: Customer confirms the booking via a subsequent voice command.

slices.title: Architecture Spike for Georgian Voice AI
slices.jtbd: When evaluating voice solutions for this epic, I want to test Georgian STT models, so that we choose a reliable engine.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given available STT APIs, When tested with Georgian audio, Then error rates are documented.
Given the findings, When concluded, Then an architecture decision record is written.

slices.title: API Contract for Voice Processing
slices.jtbd: When defining the voice feature for this epic, I want a shared contract, so that client audio streams and server intents are aligned.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the voice API spec, When a stream starts, Then the payload includes audio metadata.
Given a parsed intent, When returned to the client, Then it conforms to the unified booking DTO.

slices.title: AI Pipeline for Georgian STT and Intent Parsing
slices.jtbd: When building the AI module for this epic, I want to parse Georgian intents, so that free text maps to booking parameters.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a Georgian audio file, When processed, Then the correct service and time intent are extracted.
Given ambiguous speech, When parsed, Then a low-confidence flag is raised.

slices.title: API Bridge for Voice Commands
slices.jtbd: When connecting voice to the engine for this epic, I want to handle TTS generation, so that users get audio feedback.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a proposed slot, When sent to the bridge, Then a synthesized Georgian audio response is returned.
Given a voice confirmation, When processed, Then the booking is marked complete.

slices.title: Voice Interaction Client UI
slices.jtbd: When building the voice frontend for this epic, I want microphone capture, so that users can speak their requests.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the web interface, When mic access is granted, Then audio streams correctly to the backend.
Given a voice recording error, When it fails, Then clear visual feedback indicates the mic issue.
Given the UI controls, When navigated, Then WCAG 2.1 AA standards are met including visible focus, labelled form controls, and 4.5:1 text contrast.

slices.title: QA for Voice Scenarios
slices.jtbd: When testing the voice feature for this epic, I want to run audio test vectors, so that the end-to-end flow is validated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given pre-recorded Georgian booking requests, When fed to the pipeline, Then bookings are created.
Given noisy audio, When tested, Then fallback behavior is verified.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: E2E success rate on test vectors

epics.title: Platform Goal Measurement and Acceptance Content
epics.jtbd: When evaluating the platform, I want to see usage metrics and realistic test content, so that business outcomes are proven and the system is demonstrable.
requirements: R1: Measure Goal-Question-Metric: Goal is to maximize successful appointments; Questions are 'How many bookings succeed?' and 'What is the no-show rate?'; Metrics are booking conversion rate and attendance rate.
R2: Deploy a reachable instance populated with realistic Georgian professionals, services, and schedules to allow full traversal of the booking path.
R3: Automated regular backups of all database state are taken, and a restore procedure is verified.

slices.title: Analytics Schema and Backup Scripts
slices.jtbd: When configuring infrastructure for this epic, I want to set up metrics storage and backup jobs, so that data is preserved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the DB cluster, When a daily backup is scheduled, Then it writes to secure blob storage.
Given a restore command, When executed, Then the database recovers fully.

slices.title: Telemetry API and Data Seeding Logic
slices.jtbd: When building core systems for this epic, I want to emit metrics and seed data, so that GQM is tracked and instances are demonstratable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh deployment, When seed scripts run, Then realistic Georgian profiles and slots are created.
Given a booking event, When processed, Then it correctly increments the GQM conversion metric.

slices.title: QA for Metrics, Seeding, and Backup Restore
slices.jtbd: When verifying infrastructure for this epic, I want to test restores and metric accuracy, so that the floors are definitively met.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a test database backup, When a restore is actively performed, Then data integrity is verified.
Given the seeded instance, When a tester browses, Then all links in the booking path are walkable.

epics.title: Privacy Compliance and Account Recovery
epics.jtbd: When using the system, I want my data rights upheld and my access secure, so that the service is legally compliant and trustworthy.
requirements: R1: Professionals and customers can request an export of their personal data.
R2: Professionals and customers can request complete erasure of their personal data.
R3: A self-service recovery path is available for locked-out accounts.
R4: Non-essential cookies and trackers require explicit opt-in consent via an established platform.

slices.title: API Contract for Privacy Requests
slices.jtbd: When implementing compliance tools for this epic, I want a clear API contract, so that export and erasure payloads are defined.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API spec, When checking the export endpoint, Then it defines a standardized JSON payload structure.
Given an erasure request, When documented, Then it specifies required authentication headers.

slices.title: Privacy and Account Recovery Backend Logic
slices.jtbd: When building the compliance backend for this epic, I want to handle data extraction and deletion, so that GDPR duties are fulfilled.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid export request, When processed, Then a complete JSON dossier of the user's data is generated.
Given a complete erasure request, When processed, Then all personal identifiers are hard-deleted or irrevocably anonymized.

slices.title: UI for Privacy Tools and Cookie Consent
slices.jtbd: When building compliance UI for this epic, I want to integrate consent and recovery, so that users can control their data.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a first-time visit, When the page loads, Then an established consent banner blocks non-essential cookies until accepted.
Given a locked account, When recovery is initiated, Then the user is guided through the self-service flow.
Given the privacy interfaces, When interacting, Then WCAG 2.1 AA standards are met including visible focus, labelled form controls, and 4.5:1 text contrast.

slices.title: QA for Privacy Compliance
slices.jtbd: When testing privacy features for this epic, I want to verify exports and deletions, so that we avoid regulatory breaches.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an erased user, When queried, Then the system returns no personal data.
Given a refused cookie consent, When browsing, Then no analytics trackers are loaded.

epics.title: Local Payments Information Flow
epics.jtbd: When a customer secures a booking, I want clear instructions for direct payment, so that I know how to complete the transaction.
epics.tocConstraintRef: UI state management for payment display
requirements: R1: During checkout, present clear instructions for paying the professional directly via TBC / Bank of Georgia transfer or cash.
R2: Professionals can mark a completed booking as paid or unpaid for their internal ledger.
R3: Payment transactions are genuinely handled completely off-platform; no on-platform payment processing is performed.

slices.title: API Contract for Ledger Updates
slices.jtbd: When implementing payment tracking for this epic, I want an agreed schema, so that frontend and backend update statuses identically.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API spec, When a payment status update is defined, Then it allows 'paid' and 'unpaid' states.
Given the spec, When querying bookings, Then payment status is included.

slices.title: Backend Logic for Payment Instructions and Ledger
slices.jtbd: When building backend support for payments for this epic, I want to store professional payment info and booking payment states, so that the ledger is accurate.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a professional's settings, When requested, Then their TBC/BOG account details are securely provided for checkout.
Given a status update, When saved, Then the ledger reflects the new state without processing a transaction.

slices.title: Checkout UI and Ledger UI
slices.jtbd: When building payment screens for this epic, I want to show instructions and ledger views, so that users understand the off-platform process.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the checkout flow, When completed, Then clear off-platform payment instructions are displayed.
Given the professional dashboard, When viewing a booking, Then the payment status can be toggled.
Given the checkout UI, When interacting, Then WCAG 2.1 AA standards are met including visible focus, labelled form controls, and 4.5:1 text contrast.
slices.tocConstraintRef: UI layout clarity for text instructions

slices.title: QA for Payment Instructions
slices.jtbd: When testing payment information for this epic, I want to verify visibility and state updates, so that expectations are correct.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a completed E2E booking, When checking the confirmation page, Then TBC/BOG details are present.
Given a professional marks a booking as paid, When queried, Then the new state persists.
